topic: Company OS and org-wide AI agent adoption for non-engineering teams
segment: founders, COOs, and ops/PM leaders rolling out Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor beyond engineering
blind_spots: Governance, compliance, and data-privacy specifics for regulated functions like finance are mentioned only abstractly.
Cost, pricing, and ROI quantification for non-engineering teams is barely addressed beyond one metrics-focused source.
Change management, training, and end-user resistance (fear, skill gaps) among non-technical staff is only lightly touched.
Little direct first-person evidence from finance, marketing, or CS practitioners themselves; most non-engineering pain is described secondhand by ops/PM leaders, vendors, or analysts.
No evidence on vendor/platform selection tradeoffs or build-vs-buy decisions from the non-engineering buyer's perspective.
Much of the 'Claude Code' evidence is engineering-tool-centric and may not cleanly generalize to non-engineering workflows.
contradictions: Framing tension: some sources locate the failure in implementation and missing context ('the tech is powerful, but the implementation is broken'), while others locate it in the technology/model reliability itself ('reliability as the #1 concern').

Optimism split: vendor/platform pieces imply a turnkey company OS can solve adoption, whereas ops/executive voices warn that no tool fixes underlying broken operations and bad data ('agents amplify the mess').
